translationRepairs: Ordered to plan how Shandong's lakes could store and release water for the grain route, he wrote: "Lakes from Nanwang to Weishan across Yanzhou and Jining are the canal's reservoirs—what older engineers called 'water cabinets'.

Ordered to plan how Shandong's lakes could store and release water for the grain route, he wrote: "Within Yanzhou and Jining, lakes such as Nanwang, Mata, Shushan, Anshan, Machang, Zhaoyang, Dushan, Weishan and Xishan all serve the canal for storing and releasing water—what older engineers called 'water cabinets'.
The idiomatic rendering collapsed the source's list of nine named lakes (南旺、馬蹋、蜀山、安山、馬場、昭陽、獨山、微山、稀山) into 'from Nanwang to Weishan', omitting seven of them; restored the full list.
He ordered subordinates to plant willows on open ground and reeds in marsh.
He has ordered subordinates to plant willows on open ground and reeds in marshland.

The unit is still inside Qi Sulei's quoted memorial (今飭屬…), so the first-person speaker is giving the order; the idiomatic rendering broke the quotation by switching to third-person narrative 'He ordered'. Rendered as continuing reported speech in the present perfect.
At Chenjiadu a dam was under construction when Songjiang prefect Zhou Zhongqian and commander Lu Zhang, supervising fascine work from boats, were drowned as the returning tide collapsed the dam.

At Chenjiadu, while a dam was under construction, Songjiang prefect Zhou Zhongqian and company commander Lu Zhang, supervising fascine work from boats, were drowned when the returning tide collapsed the dam.
千總 is a company-commander rank (a low-grade Green Standard officer), not a generic 'commander'; also clarified the clause order.
He also joined River Governor Qisuole in memorializing to strengthen both banks of the dikes, from Xingze northward to Caoxian in Shandong;
He also joined Director-General of Waterways Qi Sulei in memorializing to strengthen the dikes on both banks, on the north from Xingze to Caoxian in Shandong;
Qi Sulei's name was garbled as 'Qisuole', inconsistent with the rest of the chapter; 河督 is the director-general of waterways.
The emperor consulted Qisuole and accepted Zeng Jun's plan.
The emperor consulted Qi Sulei and adopted Cengyun's proposal.
Garbled names: 齊蘇勒 rendered 'Qisuole' and 曾筠 (Ji Cengyun's given name) rendered as if a different person 'Zeng Jun'.
Zeng Jun begged leave to go home and finish mourning properly; the emperor graciously consented.
Cengyun earnestly asked to return home to complete the mourning period, and a gracious edict granted it.
曾筠 is Ji Cengyun's given name; 'Zeng Jun' wrongly reads it as a surname-plus-name of another person.
Gao Bin was named acting governor, but the emperor told Zeng Jun that since his home was near Huai'an he should still help manage the coming year's works from nearby.
Gao Bin was appointed to act in his place, but the emperor told Cengyun that, since his home was not far from Huai'an, he should help manage the next year's works from nearby.
曾筠 mistranslated as 'Zeng Jun'; 暫署 means acting in Cengyun's river-governor post, not a generic 'acting governor'.
In year 13 the emperor ordered Zeng Jun back to duty after his mother's funeral.
In year 13 the emperor ordered Cengyun to return to the works once his mother's burial was finished.
Zeng Jun laid out salt reforms: replace merchant patrols with official agents, crack down on smuggling, and set clear rewards and penalties for seizures.
Cengyun laid out salt reforms: replace merchant patrols with official agents, crack down on smuggling, and set clear rewards and penalties for seizures.
曾筠 (Ji Cengyun's given name) mistranslated as a different person 'Zeng Jun'.
He was also ordered worshipped alongside Jin Fu and Qisuole in the same rites.
He was also ordered worshipped in the same way, following the precedent of Jin Fu and Qi Sulei.
齊蘇勒 garbled as 'Qisuole'; 視…例 means following their precedent rather than being worshipped alongside them.
In office Zeng Jun handled state business as though it were his own family's concern.
In office Cengyun handled state business as though it were his own family's concern.
Huang accompanied Zeng Jun on river inspection tours and learned the craft of waterworks.
Huang accompanied Cengyun on river inspection tours and learned the craft of waterworks.

In spring of year 22, with his mother's health restored, Huang was made Vice Director-General of Southern Rivers. The emperor told him: "You served long at your father Zeng Jun's side on river work; what you observed there should make you more than able.

In spring of year 22, with his mother recovered from her illness, the emperor made Huang Vice Director-General of Southern Rivers and told him: "You served long at your father Cengyun's side on river work; with what you saw and heard there, mastering it should not be hard.
曾筠 mistranslated as 'Zeng Jun'; the emperor, not Huang, is the subject of 上以…授.
In the fourth month of year twenty-four, he asked to return home and observe filial mourning there.
In the fourth month of year twenty-four, he asked to return home to care for his aged mother for the rest of her life.
終養 means retiring home to care for an aged parent until death, not observing mourning (his mother was still alive until year 29).
He had eight sons. The eldest, Cheng Qian, a jinshi who reached Reader-in-Waiting, predeceased him.
He had eight sons. The eldest, Chengqian, a jinshi who reached Reader-in-Waiting, predeceased him.
承謙 is a single given name; romanize as Chengqian, not 'Cheng Qian' as if surname plus name.
His clansman Cheng En, a provincial graduate, rose to Governor-General of Eastern River Works.
His clan nephew Cheng'en, a provincial graduate, rose to Governor-General of Eastern River Works.
承恩 is a given name (Cheng'en), not 'Cheng En'; 族子 is a clan nephew rather than a generic clansman.
He also urged: "Alter the Jiangdu Guan River sluice and dredge a separate overflow channel to reduce how much Huai water entered Guan River."
He also urged: "The Gua River at Jiangdu lies low; alter its mouth and dredge a separate bypass channel to reduce the share of Huai water entering the Gua River."
瓜河 is the Gua River, mistranslated as 'Guan River'; 地勢卑下 (low-lying terrain) was omitted and the mouth (口門) was wrongly called a sluice.
In the eighth month the Xuyang and Wuzi overflow works remained unclosed. Before orders reached him, Gao Bin volunteered to ride there at once.
In the eighth month the overflow breach at Yangwu had not yet been closed. An edict was to send him to plan the repairs, but before it was issued Gao Bin asked to ride there at once to help.
陽武 is Yangwu county; 'Xuyang and Wuzi' are invented place names. The idiomatic version also lost the point that he volunteered before the order (命未下) was issued.
The Zhangjialu and canal sluice failures in guiyou year sprang from overconfidence and the complacency of old age.
The breaches at Zhangjialu and at the canal sluices in the guiyou year (Qianlong 18) came from his overconfidence and the complacency of old age.
Clarified that 癸酉 is the cyclical year of Qianlong 18, the year of the breaches described above.
His father Shuming commanded at Liangzhou.
His father Shuming was brigade-general of Liangzhou.
涼州總兵 is the substantive post of brigade-general (zongbing) of Liangzhou; 'commanded at Liangzhou' obscures the office.
In year 33 he acted as Governor-General of Huguang and also handled the duties of the Jingzhou garrison commander.
In year 33 he acted as Governor-General of Huguang and concurrently handled the affairs of the Jingzhou General.
荊州將軍 is the Manchu garrison General of Jingzhou, a specific high office, not a 'garrison commander'.
In year 9 he was named Baozhou agricultural colonization commissioner.
In year 9 he was named agricultural colonization commissioner of Bazhou.
霸州 is Bazhou; 'Baozhou' is a misromanization.
When Zhu Zao was removed, Gu was again made river director-general.
When Zhu Zao was dismissed, Gu Cong was again made river director-general.
Clarified the subject: 藻罷去 means Zhu Zao was removed and 复授 refers to Gu Cong.
In year 18, after a breach at Zhangjialu, he was sent with Minister Suhede to inspect.
In year 18, after a breach at Zhangjialu, he was sent with Minister Shuhede to inspect.
舒赫德 is Shuhede; 'Suhede' misromanizes the name used elsewhere in the chapter.
Once the Zhuhua bamboo dam at Shizi River was opened, the Yellow River current surged across the canal and made upstream towing nearly impossible for grain barges.
Once the bamboo-cage dam at Shizi River was opened, the Yellow River current surged across the canal and made towing the grain barges against the current nearly impossible.
竹絡壩 is a bamboo-cage dam; 'Zhuhua' is an invented name not in the source.
Chongming, isolated offshore, grew no rice; he asked for grain shipped from Jiangxi and Guangdong, ten thousand shi held in reserve for famine relief sale.
Chongming, isolated offshore, grew no rice; he asked that grain be bought and shipped from Jiangxi and Huguang, with ten thousand shi held in the Chongming granary for fair-price sale.
江、廣 here means Jiangxi and Huguang (the rice-surplus provinces), not Guangdong; 平糶 is fair-price sale.
Culverts under Guijen Levee once linked the Baojia River to the An River but had long been blocked.
Culverts under Guiren Levee once linked the Baojia River to the An River but had long been blocked.
歸仁堤 is Guiren Levee; 'Guijen' is a Wade-Giles-style misromanization.
Opening a branch of the Fenzilin River would split inflow to the An River and gradually ease the flooding."
Opening a branch of the Linzi River would split inflow to the An River and gradually ease the flooding."
分林子河一支 means 'divert a branch of the Linzi River'; 'Fenzilin' wrongly fuses the verb 分 into the name.
